findings.title: Backup-code login skips the password check whenever totpCode is non-empty
findings.description:
The password is verified only when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The IdP check at line 113 has the same gate. A non-empty `totpCode` (for example `"0"`) therefore skips first-factor verification. The new backup-code branch at line 131 keys only on `credentials.backupCode`. A request with a valid backup code, any non-empty `totpCode`, and an empty password logs in. Backup codes are offered as a downloadable text file, so the file plus the email address becomes account takeover.

The lost-access screen in `login.tsx` does send the password, so the intended UI flow is safe. The server does not enforce it. The same gate lets a valid TOTP code bypass the password on the existing TOTP path, so the root cause predates this diff. This diff adds a second credential that depends on it.

Fix at the gate: verify the password for CAL accounts whenever a backup code is submitted, for example by gating line 121 on `!credentials.totpCode || credentials.backupCode`. The external-IdP TOTP redirect (`totpEmail` in `login.tsx`) is the only legitimate no-password path, and it never sends a backup code. Add a test that a backup-code login without the correct password is rejected.

findings.title: Backup-code consume is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so codes can be reused under concurrency
findings.description: The user row is read at line 73, the index is checked at line 144, and the whole array is written back at lines 149-156 with an `update` keyed only on `id`. Two concurrent logins with the same valid code both pass the `indexOf` check against the same snapshot and both succeed. The single-use guarantee in `backup_code_instructions` is therefore not enforced under concurrency. Make the write conditional on the snapshot, for example `updateMany({ where: { id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes } })` and reject when the count is not 1. A transaction with a row lock also works.

findings.title: The enable-step password toggle does nothing because the caller's `type` overrides it
findings.description: The new `PasswordField` is passed `type="password"` at line 176. `PasswordField` sets `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` and then spreads `{...props}` after it (packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:35-39), so the caller's value wins. The eye button flips its icon and label, but the input stays masked. The login page uses the same component without a `type` prop, so only this new usage is affected. Remove the `type` prop at line 176.

findings.title: The show/hide toggle is removed from keyboard focus for every PasswordField in the app
findings.description: `tabIndex={-1}` is added to the visibility button in the shared `PasswordField`. Keyboard users can no longer reach it on login, signup, reset, or any other password input. The button keeps an sr-only label, so pointer and screen-reader users are unaffected, but keyboard operability is lost app-wide. This is an unrelated global change inside a backup-codes diff, with no rationale. Revert it or move it to its own change with a justification.

findings.title: Copy handler ignores clipboard failures and always shows success
findings.description: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` is neither awaited nor caught, and the success toast fires unconditionally. Where `navigator.clipboard` is undefined (non-secure origins such as plain-HTTP self-hosted addresses), the property access throws synchronously and the toast never appears. Where the write rejects, the rejection is unhandled and the success toast still shows. The Playwright copy step (`login.2fa.e2e.ts:120-121`) only waits for the toast, so it would pass even if the write failed. Await the call inside `try`, show an error toast in `catch`, and guard for a missing API.

findings.title: Backup codes can be dismissed without acknowledgement, and the parent state goes stale
findings.description: The Dialog's `onOpenChange` is wired to the parent's toggle (`apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64`), which is outside the diff but determines the behavior. Escape or the close control on the DisplayBackupCodes step closes the dialog without calling `onEnable`, so `viewer.me` is never invalidated. The 2FA switch keeps showing the old state until the query refetches. The codes exist only in component state and are never persisted in plaintext, so a reload or navigation loses them. Recovery then requires disabling and re-enabling 2FA. Guard dismissal on this step, or confirm before closing.

findings.title: An empty backup code on the login screen fails silently
findings.description: If the backup-code field is empty, `credentials.backupCode` is falsy, so `authorize` falls into the TOTP branch and throws `SecondFactorRequired` (next-auth-options.ts:157-159). The page treats that code as "show the second step" (line 156) and sets no message, so the submit appears to do nothing. The form has `noValidate` (line 188), so the input's `required` attribute does not block submission. Add a client-side check or a `MissingBackupCode` message for the lost-access path. The same silent path already exists for an empty TOTP code, and this change makes it reachable from a new screen.

findings.title: Test fixture `mockUser: User` lacks the new `backupCodes` field
findings.description: The fixture is typed as Prisma's `User` (line 5). Prisma types the nullable `backupCodes` as a required `string | null`, and this literal does not set it. The `twoFactorSecret: null` sibling at line 87 shows the file mirrors the schema. This should fail the type-check once the Prisma client is regenerated. I could not run `tsc` to confirm. `builder.ts` received the field in this diff, but this fixture did not. Add `backupCodes: null`.

findings.title: `BackupCode.tsx` exports a component named `TwoFactor`
findings.description: The file is named for backup codes, but its default export is `function TwoFactor(...)`, the same name as the TOTP component. It renders as `TwoFactor` in React DevTools and stack traces. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

findings.title: E2E assertion can never fail, and the diff annotates it without fixing it
findings.description: `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` passes a Promise to `expect`. A Promise is always truthy, so the check cannot fail. The FIXME added in this diff acknowledges this and points at the working pattern, but the broken assertion stays. Replace it with `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch][data-state="checked"]')).toBeVisible();`, which the test already uses at line 127.

findings.title: Backup-code verification, consumption, and disable paths have no automated tests
findings.description: A search for test files referencing backup codes, `authorize`, or the two-factor endpoints returns nothing. The only e2e additions cover the download filename and the copy and close buttons. Untested paths include single-use consumption, wrong or missing codes, the password requirement on backup login, the disable backup branch, and setup's encryption and regeneration. The TODO at line 12 acknowledges this. Add unit tests for `authorize` and the disable handler before merge, including a case for the password gate above.

findings.title: `backupCodes` is not in the context user's omit list, unlike `twoFactorSecret`
findings.description: `CreateInnerContextOptions.user` omits `twoFactorSecret` (line 21) and other sensitive fields, but not `backupCodes`. Nothing leaks today: `getUserFromSession` in `sessionMiddleware.ts` and `meHandler` both use explicit field lists that exclude it. Add `"backupCodes"` to the omit list to match the convention and keep encrypted secrets out of the type.

findings.title: Migration timestamp predates the newest existing migration
findings.description: The folder `20230804153419` sorts before the newest existing migration, `20230828094603_add_include_calendar_event`. Prisma should still apply it, since it is unrecorded, but backward timestamps confuse review and tooling. Rename it to a timestamp after the latest migration before it ships to any environment.

findings.title: Backup-code strength and storage trade-offs
findings.description: Each code is 5 random bytes, which is 40 bits. Codes are stored encrypted with the app key, not hashed, so a DB dump plus the key reveals all of them. The login path is rate limited, but the disable endpoint (`disable.ts`) has no rate limit on code guesses. It does require the password for CAL accounts, which bounds the rate. Consider a longer code, roughly 80 bits or more, and hashing if the key is shared across environments. This is acceptable for now, but the trade-off should be documented.

findings.title: New trust-boundary inputs are untyped and unvalidated
findings.description: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` here, and `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` in `next-auth-options.ts:144`, call a string method on untrusted input. A non-string JSON value throws a TypeError, which is a 500 on disable and a generic error at login. This follows the existing pattern for `password` and `code`, so it is not a bypass. Separately, `useState([])` at `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:64` infers `never[]`, which weakens type checking on the map and key calls. Use `useState<string[]>([])`, and type the decrypted JSON as `string[]` instead of `any`.

findings.title: The `missing_backup_codes` message points to a path that does not exist for existing users
findings.description: The text says "Please generate them in your settings." Users who enabled 2FA before this change have no such path. Setup returns `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled` while 2FA is on (`setup.ts:42-44`), so the only route is disabling with TOTP and re-enabling. Reword the message to say so, or add regeneration.

findings.title: A second, unused Enable/Disable modal stack is not updated by this diff
findings.description: `apps/web/components/security/` has its own `TwoFactorAuthSection`, Enable and Disable modals, and `TwoFactorAuthAPI.ts`. Nothing imports them. The Disable modal there still calls the two-argument API. This diff changes only `components/settings/`, so the two copies will drift further. Delete the unused stack in a follow-up.

findings.title: Modal state and blob URL are not cleared on reset
findings.description: `resetState` clears the password and error but not `backupCodes` or `backupCodesUrl`, and the blob URL is never revoked on unmount. Each setup call revokes the previous URL, so the leak is bounded. The codes do remain in memory after cancel. Clear both in `resetState`, and revoke the URL in an effect cleanup.

findings.title: Login error mapping and form selection are split across two patterns
findings.description: Errors are now mapped in two places: the `errorMessages` object (lines 73-80) and a new else-if chain (lines 156-160). Line 221 nests two ternaries to choose the form. Move the new codes into `errorMessages`, and extract the second-factor view into a small component.

findings.title: The backup-code input has no accessible name
findings.description: The visible `Label` at line 13 is not associated with the input, and the input is created with `label=""` at line 19. The field therefore has no accessible name. Pass the label through `TextField`, or set `htmlFor` on the label.

findings.title: The lost-access toggle cannot submit the disable form
findings.description: The toggle sits inside `<Form>` but sets no `type`. `Button` defaults to `type = "button"` (packages/ui/components/button/Button.tsx:125), so clicking it does not submit.

findings.title: The disable endpoint checks the password before the backup-code branch
findings.description: For CAL accounts with a password, the password is verified (lines 40-45) before the backup-code branch at line 48. Backup codes are cleared when 2FA is disabled (line 107). Note that the login-path bypass in the FAIL finding is separate from this endpoint.
